note: Questions from the CBSE Class X Science board exam 2025, Q.P. code 31/1/1, published by CBSE at cbse.gov.in. Questions that need a figure or a drawing are left out (Q3, Q7, Q21, Q22, Q31, Q32, Q35(b), Q36(b)). Solutions are written for this portal and are not CBSE's official marking scheme.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Electrolysis of water is a decomposition reaction. The mass ratio (M_H : M_O) of hydrogen and oxygen gases liberated at the electrodes during electrolysis of water is :
questions.solution: 2H₂O → 2H₂ + O₂. 4 g of hydrogen is released for every 32 g of oxygen, so the mass ratio is 4 : 32 = 1 : 8. (The volume ratio is 2 : 1.)

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: The products formed when Aluminium and Magnesium are burnt in the presence of air respectively are :
questions.solution: 4Al + 3O₂ → 2Al₂O₃ and 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
Consider the following reactions :
(i) Dilute hydrochloric acid reacts with sodium hydroxide.
(ii) Magnesium oxide reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid.
(iii) Carbon dioxide reacts with sodium hydroxide.
It is found that in each case :
questions.solution: All three are acid–base (neutralisation) reactions: HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H₂O; MgO + 2HCl → MgCl₂ + H₂O; CO₂ + 2NaOH → Na₂CO₃ + H₂O. Each gives a salt and water.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Reaction between two elements A and B, forms a compound C. A loses electrons and B gains electrons. Which one of the following properties will not be shown by compound C ?
options: It is highly soluble in water.
It has weak electrostatic forces of attraction between its oppositely charged ions.
It conducts electricity in its molten state or aqueous solution.
questions.solution: C is an ionic compound. Ionic compounds have strong electrostatic forces between their ions, which is why their melting points are high.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: The metals obtained from their molten chlorides by the process of electrolytic reduction are :
questions.solution: Highly reactive metals such as sodium, calcium and magnesium are obtained by electrolysis of their molten chlorides. Calcium and magnesium are the only pair where both are such metals.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Secretion of less saliva in mouth will effect the conversion of :
options: fats into fatty acids and glycerol
questions.solution: Saliva contains salivary amylase, which breaks down starch into simple sugar.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: The plant hormone whose concentration stimulates the cells to grow longer on the side of the shoot which is away from light is :
questions.solution: Auxin diffuses to the shaded side of the shoot and makes those cells grow longer, so the shoot bends towards light.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
The correct/true statement(s) for a bisexual flower is/are :
(i) They possess both stamen and pistil.
(ii) They possess either stamen or pistil.
(iii) They exhibit either self-pollination or cross-pollination.
(iv) They cannot produce fruits on their own.
questions.solution: A bisexual flower has both stamens and pistil, and it can be either self-pollinated or cross-pollinated. Statements (ii) and (iv) describe unisexual flowers.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: If pea plants with round and green seeds (RRyy) are crossed with pea plants having wrinkled and yellow seeds (rrYY), the seeds developed by the plants of F₁ generation will be :
questions.solution: Every F₁ plant is RrYy. Round (R) and yellow (Y) are dominant, so all F₁ seeds are round and yellow.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
The breakdown of glucose has taken the following pathway :
Glucose —(a)→ Pyruvate + Energy —(b)→ Lactic acid + Energy
The sites 'a' and 'b' respectively are :
options: Mitochondria and Oxygen deficient muscle cells
Cytoplasm and Oxygen rich muscle cells
Cytoplasm and Oxygen deficient muscle cells
questions.solution: Glucose is broken into pyruvate in the cytoplasm. When oxygen is short (for example during heavy exercise), muscle cells convert pyruvate to lactic acid.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
Mirror 'X' is used to concentrate sunlight in solar furnace and Mirror 'Y' is fitted on the side of the vehicle to see the traffic behind the driver. Which of the following statements are true for the two mirrors ?
(i) The image formed by mirror 'X' is real, diminished and at its focus.
(ii) The image formed by mirror 'Y' is virtual, diminished and erect.
(iii) The image formed by mirror 'X' is virtual, diminished and erect.
(iv) The image formed by mirror 'Y' is real, diminished and at its focus.
questions.solution: X is a concave mirror: sunlight (object at infinity) forms a real, point-sized image at the focus. Y is a convex mirror, which always forms a virtual, diminished and erect image.

questions.subject: Science
questions.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.text: An old person is suffering from an eye defect caused by weakening of ciliary muscles and diminishing flexibility of the eye lens. If the defect of vision is 'a' which can be corrected by lens 'b', then 'a' and 'b' respectively are :
questions.solution: Weakening ciliary muscles and a less flexible lens with age cause presbyopia. It is often corrected with bifocal lenses.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
Which of the following groups do not constitute a food chain ?
(i) Wolf, rabbit, grass, lion
(ii) Plankton, man, grasshopper, fish
(iii) Hawk, grass, snake, grasshopper, frog
(iv) Grass, snake, wolf, tiger
questions.solution: (i) can be arranged as grass → rabbit → wolf → lion, and (iii) as grass → grasshopper → frog → snake → hawk. In (ii) and (iv) the organisms do not feed on one another in a sequence (for example, a snake does not eat grass), so they do not form food chains.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: The percentage of solar energy which is not converted into food energy by the leaves of green plants in a terrestrial ecosystem is about :
questions.solution: Green plants capture only about 1% of the sunlight falling on their leaves, so about 99% is not converted into food energy.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
Assertion (A): Decomposition reactions are generally endothermic reactions.
Reason (R): Decomposition of organic matter into compost is an exothermic process.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution: Most decomposition reactions need energy (heat, light or electricity), so A is true. Composting does release heat, so R is true, but it is an exception and does not explain A.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
Assertion (A): A human child bears all the basic features of human beings.
Reason (R): It looks exactly like its parents, showing very little variations.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution: A child inherits the basic human body design, so A is true. But sexual reproduction creates variation, so a child does not look exactly like its parents; R is false.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
Assertion (A): No two magnetic field lines are found to cross each other.
Reason (R): The compass needle cannot point towards two directions at the point of intersection of two magnetic field lines.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution: If two field lines crossed, a compass at that point would have to point in two directions at once, which is impossible. So A is true and R correctly explains it.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
Assertion (A): The amount of ozone in the atmosphere began to drop sharply in the 1980s.
Reason (R): The oxygen atoms combine with molecular oxygen to form ozone.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution: Ozone levels fell sharply in the 1980s, mainly because of CFCs, so A is true. O + O₂ → O₃ is how ozone forms, so R is true, but it does not explain the drop.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Besides minimising the loss of blood, why is it essential to plug any leak in a blood vessel ? Name the component of blood which helps in this process and state how this component perform this function.
questions.solution: A leak lowers the pressure in the circulatory system, which would make the heart's pumping inefficient (and lets germs in), so it must be plugged. Platelets do this: they circulate in the blood and, at the site of injury, help the blood to clot, which seals the leak.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
(i) The transport system in plants is relatively slower than in animals. Give reasons.
(ii) State the role of phloem in the transport of materials in plants.
questions.solution: (i) Plants do not move and many of their tissues are made of dead cells, so they need much less energy; their transport (for example water rising by transpiration pull) can be slow. (ii) Phloem carries the soluble products of photosynthesis (sucrose, amino acids) from the leaves to other parts of the plant. This translocation uses energy from ATP and can go both up and down.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: An object is placed at a distance of 60 cm from a concave lens of focal length 30 cm. Use lens formula to find the position of the image formed in this case.
questions.solution: u = −60 cm, f = −30 cm. 1/v − 1/u = 1/f gives 1/v = 1/f + 1/u = −1/30 − 1/60 = −3/60 = −1/20, so v = −20 cm. The image is 20 cm from the lens on the same side as the object (virtual and erect).

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: A wire of resistance R is cut into three equal parts. If these three parts are then joined in parallel, calculate the total resistance of the combination so formed.
questions.solution: Each part has resistance R/3. In parallel: 1/Rₚ = 3/R + 3/R + 3/R = 9/R, so Rₚ = R/9.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Define electric power. When do we say that the power consumed in an electric circuit is 1 watt ?
questions.solution: Electric power is the rate at which electrical energy is consumed (or dissipated) in a circuit: P = VI. The power is 1 watt when a current of 1 ampere flows through a device with a potential difference of 1 volt across it (1 joule per second).

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: "Excessive use of chemicals and pesticides in agriculture adversely effect the environment." Justify this statement.
questions.solution: Many pesticides are non-biodegradable. They wash into soil and water, enter food chains and build up at each level (biological magnification), harming top consumers including humans. They also kill useful organisms such as soil microbes and pollinators, and pollute soil and water bodies.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
(a) "Displacement reactions also play a key role in extracting metals in the middle of the reactivity series." Justify this statement with two examples.
(b) Why can metals high up in the reactivity series not be obtained by reduction of their oxides by carbon ?
questions.solution: (a) Oxides of moderately reactive metals can be reduced by a more reactive metal such as aluminium: Fe₂O₃ + 2Al → 2Fe + Al₂O₃ + heat (thermite reaction, used to join railway tracks) and 3MnO₂ + 4Al → 3Mn + 2Al₂O₃ + heat. (b) Metals such as sodium, calcium and aluminium have a greater affinity for oxygen than carbon, so carbon cannot remove oxygen from their oxides. They are obtained by electrolytic reduction instead.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: With the help of an activity, explain the conditions under which iron articles get rusted.
questions.solution: Take three test tubes with clean iron nails. A: nails in ordinary tap water (air and water present). B: nails in boiled distilled water with a layer of oil on top (no air). C: nails with anhydrous calcium chloride (dry air, no moisture). After a few days only the nails in A rust. So iron rusts only when both air (oxygen) and water (moisture) are present.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
(i) Name two metals which react violently with cold water. List any three observations which a student notes when these metal are dropped in a beaker containing water.
(ii) Write a test to identify the gas evolved (if any) during the reaction of these metals with water.
questions.solution: (i) Sodium and potassium. Observations: the metal reacts violently and moves around on the water; a lot of heat is produced and the evolved gas may catch fire; a hissing sound is heard; the solution formed turns red litmus blue. (ii) The gas is hydrogen: bring a burning matchstick near it and it burns with a pop sound.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
Plants have neither a nervous system nor muscles, even then they respond to stimuli. For example, the leaves of chhui-mui (touch-me-not) plant when touched begin to fold up and droop.
(a) How is the information communicated in "touch-me-not" plants ?
(b) What enables the plant cells to bring out the observable response ?
(c) Differentiate the movement mentioned above from the movement of tendrils in a pea plant.
questions.solution: (a) The plant cells pass the information from cell to cell by electrical-chemical means, since there is no specialised tissue for conduction. (b) The cells change shape by changing the amount of water in them (swelling or shrinking), which makes the leaves fold. (c) Touch-me-not: a quick movement not related to growth and not directed by the stimulus. Pea tendrils: a slow growth movement towards the support (thigmotropism), because cells on the side away from the support grow faster.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
(a) What are chromosomes ?
(b) Explain in brief how stability of DNA content of a species is ensured in sexually reproducing organisms ?
questions.solution: (a) Chromosomes are thread-like structures in the nucleus, made of DNA and proteins, that carry the genes (hereditary information). (b) Germ cells are formed by a special division (meiosis) that halves the number of chromosomes, so each gamete has half the DNA. When a male and a female gamete fuse, the zygote gets the full original number again, so the DNA content stays the same from generation to generation.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
(a) Write the relationship between resistivity and resistance of a cylindrical conductor of length l and area of cross-section A. Hence derive the SI unit of resistivity.
(b) Why are alloys used in electrical heating devices ?
questions.solution: (a) R = ρl/A, so ρ = RA/l. Unit: Ω × m² / m = Ω m (ohm metre). (b) Alloys have a higher resistivity than pure metals and do not oxidise (burn) easily at high temperatures, so they make good heating elements.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
(i) Draw two isomeric structures of Butene (C₄H₈).
(ii) Name the following compounds : (I) CH₃–CH₂–CH₂–Cl (II) CH₃–CH₂–CO–CH₃
(iii) Write the chemical equations for the following reactions. Mention one essential condition each for these reactions to take place.
(I) Ethanol undergoes complete oxidation
(II) Propene undergoes hydrogenation
(III) Ethanoic acid reacts with ethanol
questions.solution: (i) But-1-ene: CH₂=CH–CH₂–CH₃ and but-2-ene: CH₃–CH=CH–CH₃ (2-methylpropene, (CH₃)₂C=CH₂, is another). (ii) (I) Chloropropane (1-chloropropane); (II) Butanone. (iii) (I) CH₃CH₂OH + 3O₂ → 2CO₂ + 3H₂O, by burning in air (oxygen); with alkaline KMnO₄ or acidified K₂Cr₂O₇ on heating, ethanol is oxidised to ethanoic acid, CH₃COOH. (II) CH₃–CH=CH₂ + H₂ → CH₃–CH₂–CH₃, with a nickel (or palladium) catalyst. (III) CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH → CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O (esterification), warmed with a few drops of concentrated H₂SO₄.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
(i) A carbon compound X is a good solvent. On reaction with sodium, X forms two products Y and Z. Z is used to convert vegetable oil into vegetable ghee. Identify and name X, Y and Z. Also write the equation of reaction of X with sodium to justify your answer.
(ii) Write chemical equation to show what happens when ethanol :
(I) burns in oxygen/air.
(II) is heated at 443 K in excess conc. H₂SO₄.
(III) reacts with acidified potassium dichromate.
questions.solution: (i) X = ethanol, Y = sodium ethoxide, Z = hydrogen (used to hydrogenate oils). 2CH₃CH₂OH + 2Na → 2CH₃CH₂ONa + H₂. (ii) (I) C₂H₅OH + 3O₂ → 2CO₂ + 3H₂O + heat and light. (II) CH₃CH₂OH → CH₂=CH₂ + H₂O (dehydration to ethene; conc. H₂SO₄ at 443 K). (III) CH₃CH₂OH → CH₃COOH (oxidation to ethanoic acid by acidified K₂Cr₂O₇; the orange colour turns green).

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
(i) Write the functions of the following parts of human female reproductive system : (I) Ovary (II) Fallopian tube (III) Uterus
(ii) State briefly two contraceptive methods used by human males.
questions.solution: (i) (I) Ovary: produces eggs (ova) and the hormones oestrogen and progesterone. (II) Fallopian tube: carries the egg from the ovary towards the uterus; fertilisation takes place here. (III) Uterus: the zygote implants in its wall and the embryo develops there, nourished through the placenta. (ii) Condom: a barrier that stops sperm reaching the egg (and also protects against sexually transmitted infections). Vasectomy: the vas deferens is cut or blocked surgically so sperm cannot be transferred.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
(i) The power of a lens 'X' is −2.5 D. Name the lens and determine its focal length in cm. For which eye defect of vision will an optician prescribe this type of lens as a corrective lens ?
(ii) "The value of magnification 'm' for a lens is −2." Using new Cartesian Sign Convention and considering that an object is placed at a distance of 20 cm from the optical centre of this lens, state : (I) the nature of the image formed; (II) size of the image compared to the size of the object; (III) position of the image, and (IV) sign of the height of the image.
(iii) The numerical values of the focal lengths of two lenses A and B are 10 cm and 20 cm respectively. Which one of the two will show higher degree of convergence/divergence ? Give reason to justify your answer.
questions.solution: (i) Negative power means a concave (diverging) lens. f = 1/P = 1/(−2.5) m = −0.4 m = −40 cm. It corrects myopia (short-sightedness). (ii) (I) m is negative, so the image is real and inverted. (II) It is twice the size of the object (magnified). (III) m = v/u, so v = m × u = (−2)(−20 cm) = +40 cm: 40 cm on the other side of the lens. (IV) The image height is negative (below the principal axis). (iii) Lens A. Power P = 1/f, so A has 10 D and B has 5 D; the lens with the shorter focal length has greater power and bends light more.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
Seawater contains many salts dissolved in it. Common salt is separated from these salts. Deposits of solid salt are also found in several parts of the world. These large crystals are often brown due to impurities. This is called rock salt and is mined like coal. The common salt is an important raw material for chemicals of daily use.

Write balanced chemical equations to show the products formed during electrolysis of brine.
questions.solution: 2NaCl(aq) + 2H₂O(l) → 2NaOH(aq) + Cl₂(g) + H₂(g). Chlorine forms at the anode, hydrogen at the cathode, and sodium hydroxide solution near the cathode.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
Seawater contains many salts dissolved in it. Common salt is separated from these salts. Deposits of solid salt are also found in several parts of the world. These large crystals are often brown due to impurities. This is called rock salt and is mined like coal. The common salt is an important raw material for chemicals of daily use.

List two uses of any one product obtained during electrolysis of brine.
questions.solution: For example, chlorine: treating drinking water (disinfectant) and making PVC or bleaching powder. (Sodium hydroxide: soaps and detergents, paper making. Hydrogen: fuels, making margarine.)

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
Seawater contains many salts dissolved in it. Common salt is separated from these salts. The common salt is an important raw material for chemicals of daily use.

A mild non-corrosive basic salt 'A', used for faster cooking, is strongly heated to produce a compound 'B', that is used for removing permanent hardness of water. Identify A and B and also write the equation for the reaction that occurs when A is heated.
questions.solution: A = sodium hydrogencarbonate (baking soda), NaHCO₃. B = sodium carbonate, Na₂CO₃ (washing soda after recrystallisation, Na₂CO₃·10H₂O). 2NaHCO₃ → Na₂CO₃ + H₂O + CO₂ (on heating).

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
Seawater contains many salts dissolved in it. Common salt is separated from these salts. The common salt is an important raw material for chemicals of daily use.

Define water of crystallisation. Give two examples of salts that have water of crystallisation.
questions.solution: Water of crystallisation is the fixed number of water molecules present in one formula unit of a salt in its crystals. Examples: copper sulphate pentahydrate CuSO₄·5H₂O, washing soda Na₂CO₃·10H₂O, gypsum CaSO₄·2H₂O.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
The maintenance functions of all living organisms must go on even when they are not doing anything particular. Even when we are just sitting in a class or even asleep, this maintenance job has to go on. These maintenance processes require energy to prevent damage and break-down of cells and tissues, which is obtained by the individual organism from the food prepared by the autotrophs, called producers.

Name and define the process by which green plants prepare food.
questions.solution: Photosynthesis: the process in which green plants make carbohydrates (glucose) from carbon dioxide and water, using sunlight absorbed by chlorophyll, and release oxygen.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
The maintenance processes of living organisms require energy, which is obtained from the food prepared by the autotrophs, called producers.

Write chemical equation involved in the above process.
questions.solution: 6CO₂ + 12H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ + 6H₂O (in the presence of sunlight and chlorophyll).

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
The maintenance processes of living organisms require energy, which is obtained from the food prepared by the autotrophs, called producers.

State in proper sequence the events that occur in synthesis of food by desert plants.
questions.solution: Desert plants open their stomata at night, take in CO₂ and store it as an intermediate (an acid). During the day, with stomata closed: chlorophyll absorbs light energy; light energy is converted to chemical energy and water is split into hydrogen and oxygen; the stored CO₂ is released and reduced to carbohydrates.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
The maintenance processes of living organisms require energy, which is obtained from the food prepared by the autotrophs, called producers.

Explain giving reasons what happens to the rate at which the green plants will prepare food (I) during cloudy weather, and (II) when stomata get blocked due to dust.
questions.solution: (I) The rate falls, because less sunlight is available and light energy is needed for photosynthesis. (II) The rate falls, because blocked stomata let in less carbon dioxide (and gas exchange is reduced).

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
In our homes, we receive the supply of electric power through a main supply also called mains, either supported through overhead electric poles or by underground cables. In our country the potential difference between the two wires (live wire and neutral wire) of this supply is 220 V.

Write the colours of the insulation covers of the line wires through which supply comes to our homes.
questions.solution: Live wire: red (or brown). Neutral wire: black (or blue). (The earth wire is green.)

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
In our homes, we receive the supply of electric power through a main supply also called mains. In our country the potential difference between the two wires (live wire and neutral wire) of this supply is 220 V.

What should be the current rating of the electric circuit (220 V) so that an electric iron of 1 kW power rating can be operated ?
questions.solution: I = P/V = 1000 W ÷ 220 V ≈ 4.5 A, so the circuit must be rated for at least about 5 A.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
In our homes, we receive the supply of electric power through a main supply also called mains. In our country the potential difference between the two wires (live wire and neutral wire) of this supply is 220 V.

What is the function of the earth wire ? State the advantage of the earth wire in domestic electric appliances such as electric iron.
questions.solution: The earth wire gives a low-resistance path for current to flow to the earth. The metal body of an appliance such as an iron is connected to it, so if current leaks to the body it flows to the earth, the body stays at earth potential, and the user does not get a severe electric shock.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
In our homes, we receive the supply of electric power through a main supply also called mains. In our country the potential difference between the two wires (live wire and neutral wire) of this supply is 220 V.

List two precautions to be taken to avoid electrical accidents. State how these precautions prevent possible damage to the circuit/appliance.
questions.solution: 1. Use a fuse or MCB of the right rating: it melts or trips when the current becomes too high (overloading or short circuit), cutting off the supply and preventing overheating and fire. 2. Do not connect too many appliances to one socket (avoid overloading), and earth metal-bodied appliances, so excess current does not flow through the wiring or the user.
